Dos isotermas y dos adiabáticas entre un: Two isotherms and two adiabats between a hot reservoir at $T_h$ and a cold one at $T_c$. It is reversible and has the highest possible efficiency between those two temperatures:
El Otto (motor de gasolina) tiene dos ad: The Otto (petrol engine) has two adiabats and two isochores; its efficiency depends only on the compression ratio $r = V_1/V_2$: $η = 1 − r^{1 − γ}$. In the Diesel the combustion is at constant pressure, with cutoff ratio $r_c = V_3/V_2$, and it allows much higher compression ratios.
El Brayton (turbinas de gas y aviones) t: The Brayton (gas turbines and aircraft) has two adiabats and two isobars: the compressor raises the pressure by a ratio $r_p = P_2/P_1$ and $η = 1 − r_p^{−(γ − 1)/γ}$. The Stirling has two isotherms and two isochores; with a regenerator that stores the heat of one isochore and returns it in the other, it reaches the Carnot efficiency.
La entropía de un gas ideal cambia en $Δ: The entropy of an ideal gas changes by $ΔS = n C_v ln {T_b}/{T_a} + n R ln {V_b}/{V_a}$. In the T-S diagram reversible adiabats are vertical and isotherms horizontal: the Carnot cycle is a rectangle. The heat of a stage is the area under the curve, $Q = ∫ T dS$, and the enclosed area is the net work.
